trigger: the session stops resolving between caller_fn and perm_fn (two require_auth calls) on the legacy route
summary: The legacy post-row recheck makes no principal-equality check (the v1 twins refuse gate=session): an empty or changed principal with perm_fn passing reaches the chokepoint as an anonymous caller and is answered 503 no_agents instead of 403; fail-closed in every ordering
classification_rationale: Code-behaviour or coverage finding; no shipped doc claim contradicted
adjudication_rationale: Verified: caller_fn re-resolves the same request credentials through require_auth on a throwaway Response (server.cpp wf_deps.caller_fn); an unresolved session yields an empty principal with deny_all, and derive_dispatch_caller sets principal = sess.username, so a differing non-empty principal needs a session rebind. The two-line gate (caller.principal != session->username -> gate=session) was drafted and withdrawn: it also re-pins the PLAN-006 'unwired CallerFn hands dispatch an empty principal with a present-empty set' contract test and the harness default caller (which carries no principal), the unwired-caller behaviour named in the per-device dispatch visibility routed row, and authz-model.md's route-class text, so it is a reviewed change on an authorization boundary, not a final-round fold. Fail-closed today (nothing dispatches). Recorded for the owner (rejected_for_alex) beside B1/B3/SP-3; docs scoped so the same-principal sentence no longer reads as covering the legacy route.

trigger: mark_cancelled throws (allocation-class fault) inside refuse_after_row or the dispatch catch
summary: Legacy cancel_execution_row does not wrap mark_cancelled (the v1 twins do): a throw inside the refusal re-enters the dispatch catch, which calls the lambda again, and a second throw escapes the handler (httplib 500, row left running, denied row already written)
classification_rationale: Code-behaviour or coverage finding; no shipped doc claim contradicted
adjudication_rationale: Adapted: the guard goes in the shared cancel_execution_row lambda (try { mark_cancelled } catch (...) { failed }), the one place all three call sites (refusal, dispatch catch, sent==0) route through, so a throwing cancel is a failed cancel (logged and counted) and nothing escapes a catch handler. No fault seam exists on the real tracker, so it is untested here (recorded in docs/test-coverage.md). The sibling residual, a throw from the audit write or the response body inside refuse_after_row, still reaches the dispatch catch (row cancelled, generic 500, no denied row when the audit write threw); that is the handler's documented raw-audit_fn posture and is left recorded in the Resource Ledger R3 text.
